intro.title: Discover Letná Park
intro.description:
Letná Park (Letenské sady) is one of Prague's most iconic city parks, situated on the Letná hill along the eastern bank of the Vltava River. The park's viewpoint offers breathtaking panoramic views of Prague Castle, the Old Town bridges, and the meandering Vltava River, making it the perfect spot for photographing Prague's skyline.

The park is shaded by lush trees and features expansive lawns, making it a favorite relaxation spot for Prague residents. Here you'll find not only beautiful natural scenery but also the famous Letná Beer Garden, where you can enjoy Czech beer while taking in spectacular city views.

The park also preserves the giant Metronome sculpture left from the Soviet era, which has become a unique historical landmark. Whether you want to take a leisurely stroll, capture beautiful photos, or experience Czech beer culture, Letná Park is a must-visit destination.

sections.title: Historical Changes
sections.content: The history of the Letná area dates back centuries and has long been an important recreation spot for Prague citizens. During the Communist era, a massive 15-meter Stalin statue stood here but was demolished in 1962. Today, a giant Metronome sculpture stands at the original site, becoming a unique historical landmark of the area. Over time, Letná Park has gradually developed into one of Prague's most important city parks, attracting countless visitors to enjoy Prague's magnificent scenery.

sections.title: Landscape Features
sections.content: Letná Park is uniquely situated on a hill, offering a privileged geographic location. The park's viewpoint is the best place to admire Prague's skyline, offering views of Prague Castle, Charles Bridge, and the Old Town bridge cluster. The park is shaded by lush trees, with large lawns suitable for picnics and recreational activities. The famous Letná Beer Garden is one of Central Europe's largest beer gardens, where outdoor seating allows you to enjoy Czech beer while taking in the beautiful city scenery.

sections.title: Cultural Significance
sections.content: Letná Park is not only a daily recreation spot for Prague citizens but also an important cultural landmark. The giant Metronome sculpture has become a collective memory for a generation, symbolizing the changes of eras. Every summer, various cultural events and music festivals are held in the park. This is an excellent place to experience local Prague life, where you can observe Prague residents' daily leisure lifestyle and feel the city's unique cultural atmosphere.

sections.title: Core Experience
sections.content: At Letná Park, the most unforgettable experience is admiring Prague's sunset from the viewpoint. When the sun sets, Prague Castle and the red-roofed buildings of the Old Town look especially beautiful against the golden sunlight. The beer garden is an excellent place to experience Czech beer culture, where you can drink and chat with locals. The park also has children's playgrounds, jogging trails, and other facilities, making it suitable for family outings. When cherry blossoms bloom in spring and maple leaves turn red in autumn, the park presents different charming scenary.

transport.title: How to Get Here
transport.airportDesc: From Václav Havel Airport Prague (PRG), take trolleybus 59 to Nádraží Veleslavín, transfer to Metro Line A to Hradčanská station, and walk to the park.
transport.intercityDesc: From Prague Main Railway Station (Hlavní nádraží), take Metro Line C to Muzeum, transfer to Line A to Hradčanská; or take tram 26 directly to Letenské náměstí.
transport.metroDesc: Take Metro Line A to Hradčanská station, then walk about 10 minutes to the park entrance. This is the most convenient transportation option.
transport.tramDesc: Take tram routes 1, 8, 12, 25, 26 to Letenské náměstí station, then walk 5 minutes to arrive.
transport.busDesc: Take bus 131 to the Sparta stop, which is just a few minutes' walk from the park entrance.
transport.selfDriveDesc: Street parking is limited (mostly blue zones). We recommend using the paid parking near Letná Stadium or P+R facilities outside the city center.
transport.walkingDesc: Walk from Old Town about 20-30 minutes, enjoying Vltava River scenery along the way.
transport.cyclingDesc: Prague offers city bike-sharing. Cycling to the park is very convenient, and there are dedicated bike paths within the park.
transport.tipsDesc: Recommended to combine metro and walking; walking uphill from Hradčanská station offers scenic views along the way. Avoid peak hours on summer weekends.

route.title: Recommended Route
route.overview: Start from Metro Line A Hradčanská station, walk uphill to Letná Park. First head to the viewpoint to enjoy the panoramic view of Prague Castle and Vltava River, then stroll along the tree-shaded paths in the park and visit the giant Metronome sculpture. In the afternoon, you can relax at Letná Beer Garden and taste Czech beer. If time permits, you can continue to nearby Prague Castle or the Old Town. Standard visit takes 2-3 hours.
steps: Depart from Hradčanská Metro station, walk uphill to Letná Park
After arriving at the park, first head to the main viewpoint to enjoy the panoramic view of Prague Castle
Stroll along the park paths and enjoy the relaxing environment shaded by trees
Visit the giant Metronome sculpture left from the Soviet era
Enjoy lunch or afternoon tea at Letná Beer Garden, tasting Czech beer
Rest on the lawn and observe the leisure lifestyle of local people
Return to the viewpoint before sunset to capture the beautiful sunset of Prague skyline
Walk down the hill to continue exploring the Old Town or Prague Castle
supplements: The park has considerable slopes; wear comfortable walking shoes
Summer UV rays are strong; take sun protection measures
Beer garden prices are reasonable and accept credit card payment
It's windy near the viewpoint; bring a jacket
Public toilets are available in the park, near the beer garden

photoSpots.tipsContent: Sunset is the golden time for photography; Prague Castle presents charming golden colors under the sunset. Cherry blossoms in spring add a romantic atmosphere to the park. It's recommended to bring a telephoto lens for city panoramas and a wide-angle lens for park scenery. Weekends are crowded; visit on weekdays to capture empty scenes.

items.name: Ming Z.
items.text: One of the most worth-visiting places in Prague! The view from the viewpoint is stunning, with Prague Castle and Charles Bridge all in sight. The beer garden atmosphere is also super great, strongly recommend visiting at sunset.

items.name: Hua L.
items.text: A free park, but the scenery is not compromised at all. The Metronome sculpture is cool and full of historical sense. Beer garden prices are reasonable, and you can enjoy the scenery while drinking. So pleasant.

items.name: Fang W.
items.text: A photography holy land! Every angle makes a great photo. Recommended to go in the evening; Prague at sunset is incredibly beautiful. The park is large, suitable for slow exploring, allocate half a day.

items.name: Wei C.
items.text: A hidden gem of Prague. Compared to the overcrowded Old Town, it's much more refreshing here. Locals have picnics on the lawn and sunbathe, full of life atmosphere. Definitely go sit at the beer garden.

officialManagement.title: About Letná Park
officialManagement.text:
Letná Park (Letenské sady) is managed and maintained by the Prague City Parks Administration and is one of Prague's most important city parks.

As Prague's most representative urban green space, Letná Park not only provides citizens with high-quality recreational space but also serves as the best location to enjoy Prague's city scenery. The viewpoint in the park attracts countless visitors to photograph the beautiful scenery of Prague Castle and the Vltava River. Today, Letná Park has become an indispensable tourist destination in Prague, carrying the cultural memory of the city and the daily recreational life of its citizens.
